primitives.name: Exponential Weights Individual Sequence Prediction (ISP)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Aggregation strategies evaluated as pseudo-participants: Top-n (n = 1,5,10,20; average of best-scoring-so-far), Local wisdom (mean of all website forecasts), Global wisdom (mean of top-3 bookmaker-odds-implied forecasts from 18 sites), Budescu–Chen (leave-one-out contribution weights), ISP-η (exponential weights on regret, η ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1}).
primitives.latex: \hat{p}_t = \frac{\sum_j w_{j,t} f_{j,t}}{\sum_j w_{j,t}}, \quad w_{j,t} \propto \exp(\eta R_{j,t-1}); \quad R_{j,t-1} = \sum_{t_0 < t}\big[l(\hat{p}_{t_0},y_{t_0}) - l(f_{j,t_0},y_{t_0})\big].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'Time index, discrete, dimensionless', 'f_{j,t}': 'Forecast of forecaster j at time t, a probability vector on the 2-simplex, dimensionless', 'p̂_t': 'Aggregated forecast at time t, also a probability vector on the 2-simplex, dimensionless', 'w_{j,t}': 'Weight of forecaster j at time t, dimensionless', 'η': 'Learning rate, positive real number, dimensionless', 'R_{j,t-1}': 'Cumulative regret of forecaster j up to time t-1, non-negative real, dimensionless', 'l(p,q)': 'Brier loss of forecast p versus outcome q, squared Euclidean distance between probability vectors, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Brier score is proper (truth-telling optimal); forecasts are treated as fixed; regret is computed relative to each forecaster's own past predictions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When η approaches infinity, ISP becomes a deterministic maximum-weight rule; when η approaches zero, weights become uniform, reverting to simple averaging.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, ISP is a core component of ensemble learning for probabilistic game outcome forecasting. The weights w_{j,t} correspond to model confidence scores updated via log-linear dynamics, while the aggregated forecast p̂_t serves as the system's final probabilistic output for each match. The regret term implements a form of online gradient descent that adapts to the relative performance of constituent models.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking the evolution of weight distribution across models reveals shifts in relative performance; sudden concentration of weights on a single model signals overfitting or structural change.

reasoning_traces.think:
ISP is an adaptive meta-algorithm for combining forecasts or strategies in an online setting. It assigns exponentially higher weights to components (models, forecasters) whose cumulative past losses are lower, with the learning rate η controlling the aggressiveness of this adaptation. The key insight is that it achieves "no-regret" guarantees: its cumulative loss grows at most logarithmically slower than the best fixed combination in hindsight. In the context of the World Cup contest, each forecaster is a component, their submitted probabilities are predictions, and the aggregated ISP forecast competes against the entire pool of individual contributions. The paper shows that tuning η yields significant improvements over simpler averages, highlighting the value of dynamic weighting schemes over static ones. This primitive is a direct precursor to modern machine-learning ensembles and forms the basis for adaptive betting strategies.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The primitive assumes that the crowd of forecasters has heterogeneous predictive abilities and that these abilities are non-stationary (e.g., some may perform well in early rounds but not knockout stages). An opposing actor could be a rational bookmaker who observes the crowd's aggregated probabilities and exploits any predictable mispricing by placing bets on the opposite side. The ISP mechanism responds to such exploitation by redistributing weight away from losing strategies. Conversely, a forecaster might reason that submitting deliberately wrong probabilities could manipulate the aggregated result if they know their contribution will dominate; however, the ISP's adaptive nature mitigates this manipulation risk by down-weighting erratic behavior.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto condition exists if the same data used to compute the regret R_{j,t-1} is also used as the true outcome y_{t0} in the loss term, causing severe lookahead bias and rendering the regret estimate meaningless. To avoid this, the paper ensures that outcomes are only revealed after all forecasts for a match have been collected, preventing any temporal leakage. Additionally, the primitive requires that the set of base predictors is fixed; adding or removing predictors mid-stream would break the regret tracking and invalidate the weight updates.
